Tip for aspiring gamedevs: Making a game with OpenGL is like making a computer out of a bunch of wires and transistors. Sure it's possible and it feels awesome, but it'll probably take years and the result will be pretty bad.

If your goal is to make a playable game, use tools that were built on top of OpenGL, like Unity, UE4, or Monogame. If your goal is to make some kind of tool relating to gamedev, or you just want to learn how things work, then OpenGL is worth looking into.
Is MonoGame still actively maintained? I was under the impression that it had been abandoned somewhat

They weren't updating the release builds for a while, so it probably seemed abandoned, but the develop branch on GitHub has always been active, and they've made a lot of progress. Now the latest release build was published April 29th, and it's nowhere near as frustrating to work with as it was a year ago. I can actually recommend it now.
Awesome! Glad to hear it - is it Xamarin who's maintaining it or is it more community-driven these days?

That part is pretty confusing, and I don't know enough to give a concrete answer. It's part of the Mono project, which is funded by Xamarin, or something like that...

At any rate, it looks like the project leads for MonoGame are not Xamarin employees, and the contributions are from random people, so I don't think Xamarin has much involvement.

Or, if you are genuinely interested in graphics programming and like solving tough challenges, it can be great fun to write your own renderer ontop of OpenGL. After all, time spent having fun is not time wasted.
I would group that in with learning how things work, but yeah, I spent more than a year doing that. It's definitely fun.
Dude, I would love to learn how to do that sort of stuff.
I'd like to point out that Ogre3D and OpenSceneGraph are both good ways to begin programming games without directly touching OpenGL

Those wanting to learn OpenGL might instead conisder Vulkan (previously called Next Generation OpenGL Initiative) and SPIR-V. You can find more information from the GDC 2015 announcement. The SPIR-V spec is released, but the Vulkan spec is still being finalised.
If you are a beginner graphics programmer, definitely do not go and study Vulkan instead of OpenGL. The concepts learned via OpenGL are still relevant to Vulkan, whilst having easier to digest code.
